sites.site: Stuyvesant Falls Park public cartop launch context
sites.finding: The Town’s 2021 Recreation Plan documents no formal public water access within the hydroelectric project boundary and identifies surrounding impoundment/tailrace lands as private; it describes informal access at nearby locations such as Sandbar Park but does not verify a launch or lawful carry at the stored Stuyvesant Falls coordinate. The adopted 2025 plan does not establish that exact entry.
sites.sourceAction: Retained the original coordinate only as a research candidate, changed route wording so it no longer claims a verified public cartop launch or portage, and added a route hold.
sites.publicationAction: Withhold the route until a managing authority confirms the launch location and lawful carry around the falls.
sites.reopenWhen: A current manager-backed map or written public-access designation identifies the launch, legal carry, parking, and correct side of the falls.

sites.finding: USBR’s feasibility DEIS identifies Tailwaters as one of the three formal South Fork Boise launch areas, alongside Village and Danskin. The reviewed official material supports the facility identity but not a more precise GPS or surveyed wet edge than the existing control.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the existing USBR/Wilderness Portal access-area anchor and its 1,200-foot uncertainty; did not snap it to the mapped channel or a third-party ramp point.
sites.publicationAction: No new route hold; retain existing tailwater and dam-hazard caveats.
sites.reopenWhen: A current USBR/land-manager GIS feature or field-verified entry resolves the launch within the Tailwaters facility.

sites.site: NYSDEC Catharine Creek WMA south Airport/Rock Cabin Road cartop access
sites.finding: The NYSDEC Great Divide plan identifies the south-end Airport/Rock Cabin Road area as an informal hand-carry launch context; the WMA map distinguishes launch and parking areas. The source supports the access area, not the stored point as a surveyed wet edge.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the coordinate and route field checks, changed the provider role from water-entry to access-anchor, and tied its provenance to the current official plan/map.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: A current NYSDEC GIS entry or georeferenced official map isolates the wet-edge entry and carry.

sites.site: William Rhodes Island Park below-dam access / Fertile Mill Park
sites.finding: Iowa DNR FeatureServer object 275 (GlobalID ec2df35d-44b5-445b-94e9-e4415d41e108) identifies City-owned Fertile Mill Park on the Winnebago River, a natural access with gravel parking and a 13-foot parking-to-access distance. The published geometry is a defensible facility anchor; it is not a surveyed wet edge. City materials identify William Rhodes Island Park at the Fertile Dam, so the safe below-dam side must still be confirmed.
sites.sourceAction: Updated route and trip-detail coordinates to the live DNR feature, labeled the point as a natural access-area anchor, retained the dam exclusion, and corrected the saved source snapshot from an HTML directory response to the verified JSON feature query.
sites.publicationAction: Temporarily withhold the route because canonical geometry could not be regenerated without @paddletoday/geo; corrected source remains available for regeneration.
sites.reopenWhen: Regenerate and audit the canonical route geometry/catalog from the corrected access anchor, then verify safe below-dam entry and the Mason City take-out.

sites.site: Kemps Mill Park walk-in Conococheague access
sites.finding: Maryland DNR explicitly identifies public walk-in access at Kemps Mill Park. The park location does not establish a developed boat ramp, and the route already describes it as walk-in access with field confirmation.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the conservative park/access anchor and the walk-in-only caveat; no coordinate snap to hydrography.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: A current park map or field check identifies a better exact water-entry point and confirms permitted carry.

sites.finding: The 2021 North Branch guide publishes the PFBC Sayre Access GPS at river mile 290.5. The stored coordinate landed on a different waterway several miles west. The 2008 PFBC Section 1 table prints a conflicting coordinate; the newer guide GPS and route-mile context support the mainstem access.
sites.sourceAction: Updated the route and all trip-detail copies to the 2021 guide GPS, added an authoritative access-anchor control with published source hash, and documented the older-table conflict.
sites.publicationAction: Temporarily withhold both dependent routes until their canonical geometries/catalog are regenerated; @paddletoday/geo is missing.
sites.reopenWhen: Regenerate and audit both route geometries from the corrected shared Sayre start, then verify each route remains aligned with its named mainstem endpoints.

sites.site: Catoctin Creek Park & Nature Center water access
sites.finding: The current Frederick County park map marks Water Access locations in the park but does not publish georeferenced coordinates for an individual ramp or bank entry. Existing coordinate remains a park/access-area anchor shared by the two route occurrences.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the conservative shared access anchor; did not infer an exact point from an unreferenced map image.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: A current county GIS feature or georeferenced map ties the named access symbol to a coordinate and route role.

sites.site: W. Locust Street Union Bridge access anchor
sites.finding: Carroll County’s current water-trails page identifies kayaking at W. Locust Street, describes ample parking, and directs users down steps or a slide on a steep bank. It supports public access context but not a surveyed wet-edge coordinate.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the 800-foot near-water anchor and updated the control method/hash to cite the current county description rather than relying on American Whitewater for the access evidence.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: A county GIS point or field-verified landing identifies the waterline and lawful carry more precisely.

sites.site: County Highway K Plover River canoe access
sites.finding: Portage County describes a small county highway right-of-way with canoe access on Plover River at Highway K, but does not publish a precise GPS entry point. The stored bridge-area coordinate is an approximate access anchor, not a proven water-entry point.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the coordinate, added a county-source access-anchor control with 800-foot uncertainty, and changed route/detail names and notes so they no longer imply a developed bridge launch or exact wet edge.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: A current county GIS feature or field check locates the right-of-way, legal parking, carry, and water entry.

sites.site: NYSDEC Fish Creek WMA Pope Mills / Route 58 hand launch
sites.finding: The NYSDEC WMA page supports hand-launch recreation. The current launch directory lists the Pope Mills / Route 58 access with five-car parking and a 0.8-mile hand carry; the published point is therefore an access/carry anchor and should not be presented as a surveyed shoreline entry.
sites.sourceAction: Kept the coordinate, corrected the provider role from water-entry to access-anchor, and named the 0.8-mile carry in the terminal/access-point label and note.
sites.publicationAction: No coordinate change or route hold.
sites.reopenWhen: Current DEC GIS or field verification ties the listed coordinate to the signed carry endpoint and exact public water entry.
